author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Canada imposed tariffs Tuesday on about $20 billion worth of U.S. goods after the latest escalation in the trade dispute with Washington, according to an Associated Press report carried by New Hampshire Public Radio.

The measures cover hundreds of American products, including steel, aluminum, cheese, appliances, clothing, cosmetics and farm equipment. Canadian officials said the tariffs match U.S. measures dollar for dollar and rate for rate, taking effect at 12:01 a.m. Tuesday.

The immediate national impact may be limited, but RBC Economics said some businesses could be hit hard. The dispute matters in New Hampshire because manufacturers, retailers, farmers and tourism operators all operate in a region where cross-border commerce and Canadian visitors are part of the economic picture.

The AP reported that the two countries’ supply chains remain deeply integrated and that Washington has threatened additional tariffs on Canadian vehicles, auto parts and steel next year. The next round of negotiations will determine whether Tuesday’s action remains a pressure tactic or becomes a longer disruption.
dek: Ottawa imposed tariffs on about $20 billion in U.S. goods Tuesday, adding fresh uncertainty for a New Hampshire economy tied to its northern neighbor.
headline: Canada’s new tariffs put New Hampshire trade links in focus
sourceName: New Hampshire Public Radio / Associated Press
